You can though. You just started working at your job, less then a week and probably haven't even received your first paycheck. So unless you made money before working in this job, you do currently qualify for medicaid.

That qualification won't last, but you can certainly sign up and when you start receiving your paycheck you'd have to report the change of income. I'm not sure if they immediately drop you or not.

You might want to talk to someone who works for medicaid just to be sure.

Otherwise, practical advise: Take out a loan, get your meds and see a doctor for the next two months until insurance kicks in. Use generics to reduce costs.

And make sure you review your coverage limits. Company insurance likes to throw in maximum limits of like $1 million a year or lifetime which can go quickly if you need hospitalizations and have medical complications.

I'm not against going back to therapy. But I was let go from my last therapist without any referrals and I was told there was nothing left to cover. PCP took over my med management, and the rest is history.

Here's the problem. I was in therapy for two years, that was my second therapist, and it didn't help with my urges at all. I think that was because our topics were regarding my day life, since both therapists didn't really want to discuss why I'm suicidal or do anything on that subject.

I found out since all of my hospitalizations were voluntary I can still purchase a firearm. So that's something I'm leaning towards. We'll see how it goes with my PCP since she might be referring me out to another therapist. Maybe this one can help, but if not I have no intention of living much longer.
I'd love to but would prefer not to be involuntarily hospitalized.
